findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot sort by datetime; endpoint 500s
findings.body: The audit log endpoint now routes requests with `optimized_pagination=true` to `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by="-datetime"`, but `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` (src/sentry/api/paginator.py line 838) is copied from the numeric `Paginator` and calls `math.floor(value)` / `math.ceil(value)` on the key. For `AuditLogEntry.datetime` that value is a `datetime`, so `math.floor` raises `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime`. Any request that passes `optimized_pagination=true` (and satisfies the admin check) will fail with a 500 as soon as `build_cursor` computes cursor keys. The previous code path used `DateTimePaginator`, which converts datetimes to timestamps.

findings.title: Negative-offset "advanced feature" crashes: Django does not support negative slicing
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is true and a caller supplies a cursor with a negative offset (possible now because `Cursor.from_string` happily parses a negative offset from the `value:offset:is_prev` string), the code does `queryset[cursor.offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django's ORM does not support negative indexing — `QuerySet.__getitem__` raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported`. The comment claiming "the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is false, so instead of crashing this will surface as a 500 for any user-supplied cursor with a negative offset. There is also no validation anywhere that a client-supplied cursor offset is non-negative, which is a security/robustness regression on a public API endpoint.

findings.title: BasePaginator change silently drops negative offsets for forward cursors, but still passes them for prev cursors
findings.body: The change `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` alters `BasePaginator` behavior for all existing paginators: for forward cursors a negative offset is now silently clamped to 0, while for `is_prev` cursors a negative offset is still passed straight into the queryset slice, where Django raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported`. Since client-supplied cursor strings are parsed into arbitrary integer offsets (`Cursor.from_string` accepts negative values), a crafted or corrupted prev-cursor (`...: -5:1`) will now crash any endpoint using `BasePaginator`/`DateTimePaginator`/`Paginator`, not just the new optimized path. The offset should be validated/clamped in both branches.

findings.title: Redirect resolution depth reduced from 10000 to 1000 without handling the truncated case
findings.body: The redirect-following loop limit was lowered from 10000 to 1000. When the redirect chain exceeds 1000 hops, the loop simply ends with `set_span_id` pointing at an intermediate node rather than the true set root. The script then does `hset main_redirect_key span_id set_span_id` and merges the span into whatever set that intermediate id resolves to, so a very deep segment tree gets split into two segments that are never rejoined (the old comment explicitly documented this failure mode at depth 10k). There is no metric, error, or fallback when the limit is hit, making the split silent. If the reduction was intentional for latency, the depth-limit-exceeded case should at least be observable.

findings.title: New hard 1000-span eviction silently drops spans, possibly including the root span
findings.body: The script now evicts with `zpopmin` whenever a set exceeds 1000 members. ZPOPMIN removes the lowest-scored members (earliest `end_timestamp_precise`), which may include the segment's root span — evicting it does not clear the `span-buf:hrs:` flag, so the segment will still be treated as having a root but will flush without one, producing an incomplete segment. Additionally, evicted spans are dropped permanently with no metric, log, or outcome emitted, so data loss from oversized segments is invisible. The old behavior flushed oversized segments intact and only skipped them (with an error log and `segment_span_count_exceeded` metric) when reading — that check was removed in buffer.py without a replacement, so `max_segment_spans` is now a dead constructor parameter and the only guard against huge segments is this silent truncation.

findings.title: Module docstring still describes the buffer as sets, not sorted sets
findings.body: The module docstring (and the glossary at line 58, "span-buf:s:* -- the actual set keys, containing span payloads") still describes the segment store as Redis sets and describes step 3 as adding payloads to a "set". After this change the keys are sorted sets scored by `end_timestamp_precise`, and the redirect/merge logic in add-buffer.lua uses ZUNIONSTORE/ZPOPMIN. The stale documentation will mislead anyone reasoning about ordering, eviction, or the max-segment-size behavior.

findings.title: Unrelated, undocumented audit-log endpoint behavior change in a spans-buffer PR
findings.body: This PR (titled/described as a spans buffer optimization) adds a new query parameter `optimized_pagination` to the audit log endpoint that switches pagination behavior based on a client-controlled flag, gated only on `is_superuser` or `member.has_global_access`. Aside from being broken (see OptimizedCursorPaginator datetime issue), it changes a public API contract with no tests, no changelog, and no relationship to the PR's stated purpose. It should be split out or removed.
